thread:
Jordan Blake: Heads up: Marketplace partner is asking if they can reuse our standardized security/RFP language for partner-led deals.

They’re filling out a marketplace security questionnaire (their portal) and want “approved Redwood answers” they can paste in. Can we point them at the new RFP response library + any do/don’t guidance?

Markus Klein: +1 seeing this a lot with cloud marketplaces. Usually they want:
- SOC 2 type/scope
- encryption at rest/in transit
- SSO/SAML/SCIM
- audit logs
- data retention/residency

We should give them language but also guardrails (don’t overcommit, don’t share evidence, don’t promise roadmap).

Naomi Feldman: Yep. They can reuse the approved boilerplate from the canonical library, but we should NOT have partners improvising or summarizing evidence artifacts.

Recommended guidance:
1) Use the “standard-rfp-response-library” answers verbatim (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private variants).
2) Do not attach SOC 2 report / pen test docs in partner portals. Route those requests via GRC (NDA + tracking).
3) If the portal forces a yes/no that’s ambiguous, loop us in before submitting.

Can someone drop the link + the exact snippet to send?

Daniel Carter: Here’s the internal canonical source (approved language + evidence pointer mapping):
- Confluence: /sales-enablement/security-faq/standard-rfp-response-library

And the field package (PDFs) is in the GTM shared drive as “Security Enablement Kit v2” (same content, just formatted). If they need “public-safe” language only, we should use the public security overview / high-level FAQ (docs site) vs the full internal FAQ.

Also: if they request SOC 2 report, process is: NDA -> GRC approval -> secure share link. We track recipients.

Olga Petrov: +1. Please make sure the guidance explicitly says:
- Partners should not claim we “certify” their marketplace offering.
- Don’t commit to specific incident notification timelines unless it’s in the customer contract / order form (use the approved incident notification wording).

If they’re asking for “pen test report”, we only share summary (if any), and only under NDA.

Isabelle Laurent: For partner-led deals, do we want a single “latest kit link” we can send? I can add a CRM snippet / template in HubSpot later, but need the canonical URL + the access model.

Naomi Feldman: Let’s keep “source of truth” = Confluence page, and “send to partner” = Drive PDF pack link (view-only) IF they’re a trusted partner + we’re OK with them distributing. Otherwise, send them the public-safe docs only.

For now, I’d tell the partner:
- Use RFP library boilerplate for questionnaire responses
- Do not share restricted evidence
- For SOC 2 requests, introduce Redwood GRC

Soojin Lee: I can draft a short partner-facing blurb for Partnerships to paste into email/Slack.

Something like:
“Feel free to reuse Redwood’s approved security questionnaire language from our RFP response library. Please use the wording as-is and avoid attaching restricted evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test details) in marketplace portals; we can provide those artifacts under NDA via our compliance team upon request.”

Markus Klein: Works. Also call out they should choose the right deployment mode language. Marketplace usually implies Hosted, but some partner deals are Dedicated/Private. I’ve seen partners copy Private answers into Hosted questionnaires and it confuses reviewers.

Daniel Carter: Here’s a specific snippet you can use (safe + accurate):
- “Redwood Inference supports multiple deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments in customer-controlled environments). Security controls and shared responsibility differ by deployment. For this questionnaire response, please specify which deployment applies.”

And: “SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA upon request.”

Olga Petrov: Please don’t say “available upon request” without the NDA qualifier. Suggested wording: “SOC 2 Type II report may be shared under NDA through Redwood’s compliance team.”

Naomi Feldman: Good catch. Let’s lock wording:
- “SOC 2 Type II report may be shared under NDA through Redwood’s compliance team.”

Jordan Blake: Great. Action items:
1) @Soojin Lee please send the partner-facing blurb + include the “pick the right deployment mode” reminder.
2) @Isabelle Laurent once we decide the final distribution link, add a HubSpot snippet/template for partner-led marketplace questionnaires.

For now I’ll reply to the partner: reuse approved RFP library language, and loop Redwood GRC for evidence.

Soojin Lee: On it. Will post the blurb here in ~30.

Soojin Lee (later): Draft to send (feel free to edit):

“Thanks — yes, you can reuse Redwood’s approved security questionnaire language from our standardized RFP response library. Please copy responses verbatim and select the correct deployment mode (Hosted, Dedicated, or Private), since shared responsibility differs by deployment. 

Please do not upload restricted evidence (e.g., SOC 2 report, penetration testing materials) into marketplace portals. Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report may be shared under NDA through Redwood’s compliance team; if you need artifacts, we’ll coordinate the request and provide the approved materials via secure sharing.”

Naomi Feldman: Approved from my side. :thumbsup:

Olga Petrov: Approved. :thumbsup: (and thanks for the NDA language)

Markus Klein: Looks good. If they ask “Do you store customer prompts?” / retention questions, point them to the retention one-pager and make sure they don’t answer beyond what’s in the library.

Jordan Blake: Sent. Thanks all.
